# `bin` commands

## `bin activate`

Make an inactive bin available again for stock lines and transfers.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | item |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/bin.activate` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow bin activate A3:Top --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Shelf back in use" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "bin activate", "input": {"bin": "A3:Top"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bin` | `BIN` | string | yes | no | — | Bin id, full name (A:3:Top) or label code.; minimum length 1; maximum length 1004 |
| `site` | `--site` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Site the bin is at, by id or name; omitted, the bin is found by id, or by a name or label only one site has. |
| `expected_version` | `--expected-version` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | — |

### Command and context options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Print one JSON object. |
| `--data-root TEXT` | Data root; otherwise `BOOKFLOW_DATA_ROOT`, then `~/.bookflow`. |
| `--dry-run` | Validate and preview without writing. |
| `--reason TEXT` | Short reason for the write. |
| `--source-ref TEXT` | Identifier of the source that triggered the write. |
| `--interactive` | Prompt for input fields not supplied as arguments or options. |
| `--directive TEXT` | Standing-instruction code or id cited by the write. |
| `--idempotency-key TEXT` | Retry-safe key for this create command. |
| `--company TEXT` | Company id, `Organization/Company`, or display name. |

### HTTP

Route: `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/bin.activate`

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.

| Header | Requirement | Meaning |

| `Authorization` | required for bearer clients | `Bearer <secret>` |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Name` | optional | Stable caller name recorded in audit |

## `bin create`

Add a bin to a site that tracks bins, as the anchor's Advanced Inventory bin locations do: up to three levels (an aisle, a shelf, a section -- A, A:3, A:3:Top), each named once per site, with an optional label code a scanner reads. Turn bins on for a site first with `inventory-site update <site> --tracks-bins true`. Example: `bookflow bin create --site Warehouse --name 3 --parent A --barcode 2000000000107`.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | item |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/bin.create` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow bin create --site Warehouse --name Top --parent A3 --barcode 2000000001036 --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Top shelf of bay A3" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "bin create", "input": {"site": "Warehouse", "name": "Top", "parent": "A3", "barcode": "2000000001036"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `site` | `--site` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Site the bin is at, by id or name; omitted, the default site. The site must track bins. |
| `name` | `--name` | string | yes | no | — | This level of the bin name, such as "A", "3" or "Top" (no colons).; minimum length 1; maximum length 200 |
| `parent` | `--parent` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Enclosing bin at the same site, by id or full name such as "A:3"; bins go three levels deep. |
| `barcode` | `--barcode` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Label code a scanner reads; unique among active bins. |
| `description` | `--description` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |

## `bin deactivate`

Make a bin inactive so new stock lines cannot name it. Refused (E_RECORD_IN_USE, naming the items) while it or a bin inside it holds stock, or while active bins sit inside it.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

## `bin show`

Show a bin with what it and the bins inside it hold (item, lot or serial number, quantity), as of today or as_of. A bin is named by id, full name (A:3:Top) or label code; name the site when two sites have a bin of that name.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | read |
| Required role | member |
| Capability | item |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/bin.show` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow bin show A2 --site Warehouse --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

## `bin update`

Rename a bin (the bins inside it are renamed with it), or change its label code or description. A bin keeps its site and level.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | item |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/bin.update` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow bin update A3 --site Warehouse --description "Kits and fittings" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Bay contents changed" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "bin update", "input": {"bin": "A3", "site": "Warehouse", "description": "Kits and fittings"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |

| `site` | `--site` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Site the bin is at, by id or name; omitted, the bin is found by id, or by a name or label only one site has. |

| `name` | `--name` | string \| null | no | yes | null | New name for this level; the bins inside it are renamed with it. |
